MEMORANDUM OF LAW

IN THE MATTER OF: State v. Anderson, Case No. 2026-CR-04517

STATEMENT OF FACTS

On January 15, 2026, the defendant, John Anderson, was observed by Officer Martinez (Badge #4421) operating a motor vehicle on Highway 101 near the intersection of Oak Street. The officer initiated a traffic stop after observing the vehicle crossing the center line on three occasions within a quarter-mile span.

Upon approach, Officer Martinez detected a strong odor of alcohol emanating from the vehicle. The defendant exhibited slurred speech and bloodshot eyes. A field sobriety test was administered pursuant to 42 U.S.C. § 1983, and the defendant failed two of three standardized tests.

LEGAL ANALYSIS

Under the Fourth Amendment to the United States Constitution, a traffic stop constitutes a seizure. See Terry v. Ohio, 392 U.S. 1 (1968). The stop must be supported by reasonable suspicion of criminal activity. Illinois v. Wardlow, 528 U.S. 119 (2000).

The prosecution bears the burden of proving beyond a reasonable doubt that the defendant operated a motor vehicle while under the influence, in violation of Cal. Veh. Code § 23152(a).

CONCLUSION

Based on the foregoing analysis, the evidence supports the charges as filed. The officer's observations provide sufficient probable cause for the arrest under established Fourth Amendment jurisprudence.

Respectfully submitted,
District Attorney's Office
March 26, 2026
